clue.text: Urban area: it's found within country's borders

indicators.note: found within says one piece sits inside the other
the borders of a word are its first and last letters, the outer edge of country

parts.note: the word country, whose outside letters are taken
it, with the 's read as 'is' joining it to the indicator

explanation.surface: A geography note: a town lies inside a nation's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The borders of 'country' are C and Y; IT goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A city is the standard example of a large built-up, urban settlement.

clue.text: Never frantic, when upset about new spice

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces surround the new letter
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, reading from the bottom up

parts.note: no can mean never, as in 'no way'
manic means frantic

explanation.surface: Someone told to stay calm when upset about a new seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Never' gives NO as in 'no way'; in a down clue 'upset' turns the pair bottom to top before the new letter goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnamon is a sweet spice made from the dried bark of an Asian tree.

clue.text: Some late trading will get you fish

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Market traders working late are promised a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetra is a small brightly coloured tropical freshwater fish popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Doctor attending one in a game finishing early? That's exciting

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so the doctor goes alongside the rest
in says the one goes inside the shortened game
finishing early means the game stops before its last letter

parts.note: a match is a game, as in a tennis match
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A medic watching a match that is cut short, which the setter calls thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is a link pointing to the definition; the question mark flags that the game is cut short only in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramatic and exciting both describe events that are thrilling, sudden or striking to watch.

clue.text: Match official in tie finally to improve

parts.note: ref is short for referee

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word next to it

parts.note: the word tie, whose last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A referee in a drawn game trying to raise standards.
explanation.definitionFit: To refine is to improve something by removing flaws or impurities.

clue.text: Spoils question about shops offering confectionery

parts.note: mars means spoils or ruins

indicators.note: about says the question wraps around the shops

parts.note: how is a question word
a mall is a set of shops

explanation.surface: Ruining an inquiry into what the shops sell in sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshmallow is a soft spongy sweet made from sugar and gelatine.

clue.text: Pinch place after elevating skill in bowling?

indicators.note: elevating means lifting up, so in a down clue the pair reads from the bottom up

parts.note: nip means pinch
a spot is a place

explanation.surface: Finding the right place to grip the ball before bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: NIPSPOT read upwards. Bowling here is cricket bowling, where the bowler delivers the ball overarm to the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Topspin is a forward rotation a bowler imparts to make the ball dip and bounce sharply.

clue.text: Creation of Morse concerns Oxford detective Endeavour, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letters of the four words are taken

explanation.surface: A query about the TV detective Endeavour Morse, who works in Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Endeavour Morse, the TV detective; the definition means Samuel Morse, inventor of the telegraph alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Morse devised the dot-and-dash telegraph code that bears his name.

clue.text: 50 per cent off? I'll take that!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally the opposite of half, taken whimsically as not being a half-price deal
second meaning: British slang for 'very much so!', an emphatic yes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British colloquial for 'absolutely!'; read literally it denies that something is halved.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal British exclamation of enthusiastic agreement, and literally negates a halving.

clue.text: Military advisors run off after ideas misfiring

indicators.note: after puts running off behind the rearranged ideas
misfiring means going wrong, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters of ideas, rearranged
to decamp is to run off or leave suddenly

explanation.surface: Officers fleeing once their plans go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Aides-de-camp are officers who act as personal assistants to senior commanders.

clue.text: Quick assault seizing power

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the assault encloses power

parts.note: a raid is a sudden assault
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A swift attack that takes control of a power station or regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and quick are synonyms describing great speed.

clue.text: A group of Titanic's musicians, possibly, and call to them?

definitions.text: A group of Titanic's musicians, possibly
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: a band on a ship, as the Titanic's band famously played on
second meaning: the order given to everyone aboard a sinking vessel to leave it

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase splits as A BAND ON SHIP for the musicians; whole, it is the order to leave a sinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The captain's emergency command to evacuate a vessel, which the Titanic's band famously did not heed.

clue.text: Transient matters that man initially managed in record time

indicators.note: in places the man and the letter inside the record and time

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
an era is a period of time
he means that man

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word after it

parts.note: the word managed, whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone completing fleeting tasks remarkably quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are things of passing interest, lasting only a short while.

clue.text: Be against attitude presented by musical work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a numbered musical work
a pose is an attitude struck, a posture

explanation.surface: Objecting to a stance taken in a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose is to resist or argue against something, the verb meaning to take the other side.

clue.text: Advertise seaside attraction, observe, not the first

parts.note: a prom is a promenade along a seafront

indicators.note: not the first says the opening letter is removed

parts.note: to note is to observe

explanation.surface: Plugging a seafront walk and urging people to see it.
explanation.definitionFit: To promote a product is to publicise it to boost sales.

clue.text: Soldier laid back in beret for a quick snooze

indicators.note: in puts the reversed soldier inside the beret

parts.note: a beret is a kind of cap

indicators.note: laid back means set down backwards, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so soldier gives the insect

explanation.surface: A relaxed soldier with his beret on, dozing off.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier is an insect, not a GI or a member of the Territorial Army: a soldier ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short light sleep taken during the day, a brief doze.

clue.text: Area of Russia, not Southern European region

indicators.note: not means without, so the southern letter is taken away

parts.note: Siberia is the vast Asian region of Russia

explanation.surface: Distinguishing a Russian territory from a southern European one.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula in south-western Europe holding Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: Fail to stay upright, being voluble in ocean, swimming

indicators.note: in places the talkative word inside the rearranged sea
swimming suggests the letters move about freely

parts.note: the letters of ocean, rearranged
being voluble means using many words, being verbal

explanation.surface: A chatty swimmer in the sea, losing balance in the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being voluble' looks like a description of the swimmer, but it is a synonym piece: talkative, wordy.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbalance is to lose one's equilibrium and topple over.

clue.text: Refusal is beginning to elicit uproar

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the word elicit, whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Saying no starts to provoke an outcry.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise and uproar both mean a loud disturbance or din.

clue.text: Power supplied by piece of legislation and treaty

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
an act is a law passed by parliament

explanation.surface: Authority granted by a statute and an international agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement between parties, such as nations.

clue.text: A local name for European city displaying a certain atmosphere

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name for Rome

explanation.surface: A city known by its native name gives off a particular feel.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a smell that pervades a place, giving it a particular air.

clue.text: Revise legal document in Early English, putting King foremost

indicators.note: foremost puts the king at the very front of the rest

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: in puts the legal document inside Early English

parts.note: EE is the abbreviation for Early English, the medieval architectural style
a writ is a legal document issued by a court

explanation.surface: Redrafting an old legal text with the monarch's name moved to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To rewrite something is to revise it by writing it again in altered form.

clue.text: The favourable slant is overwhelming a stage performer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: overwhelming means engulfing, so the spin surrounds the letter A

parts.note: spin is a favourable slant put on news

explanation.surface: A PR angle overpowering an actor's image.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, after Thespis, the legendary first actor of Greek drama.

clue.text: Risk taken with article still being tested?

parts.note: to bet is to risk money on an outcome
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A gamble paired with a product still under trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Software in beta is in its trial release, being tried out by users before full launch.
